structured_output.summary: The change implements DisposableStack.prototype.adopt in its own file, following all eight spec steps in order. Step 2 uses require_disposable_stack with ?, step 3 throws a ReferenceError when disposed, step 4 throws a TypeError when onDispose is not callable, and step 5 is a builtin closure that captures value and onDispose in its slots and calls ops::call(onDispose, undefined, [value]) with the result propagated. Step 6 creates the function with an empty name and length 0. Step 7 calls add_disposable_resource with ? and undefined as the value, sync kind and the function as the method. Step 8 returns value. No test-shaped branches, no swallowed errors, no default return values. The only open item is the lint flag on an expect() inside the closure, which is an invariant that holds while a built-in runs, so it is not a defect in itself.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Non-blocking: (1) adopt_closure uses agent.active_function().expect("a running built-in"). This is an invariant rather than a reachable user error, but the lint flags it. If the codebase has a non-panicking accessor or a convention for built-in closures, prefer it. (2) The intro sentence "This method performs the following steps when called:" from the stub was removed. Restoring it is optional. Otherwise the implementation looks complete for the adopt target.
